_note: Transparent, hand-authored screening knowledge base for BookMyCare. Weights are expert-style heuristics chosen for an explainable prototype, NOT clinically validated parameters. Outputs are screening suggestions for discussion with a clinician, never diagnoses.

conditions.name: Common cold (viral upper respiratory infection)
conditions.description: A mild viral infection of the nose and throat that usually settles within 7-10 days.
self_care: Rest and drink plenty of fluids
Warm saline gargles or honey-lemon drinks may ease a sore throat
Wash hands often to avoid spreading the infection
see_doctor_if: Symptoms last more than 10 days or get worse after improving
High fever, breathing difficulty or chest pain develops

conditions.name: Influenza (flu)
conditions.description: A viral respiratory infection with sudden fever, aches and cough; most people recover in about a week.
suggested_tests: Influenza rapid antigen / PCR test (if advised)
self_care: Rest at home and avoid contact with others while feverish
Drink plenty of fluids
Monitor temperature and breathing
see_doctor_if: You are pregnant, over 65, or have a chronic condition (higher risk of complications)
Breathing difficulty, chest pain, confusion or symptoms that improve then return worse

conditions.name: COVID-19
conditions.description: A viral respiratory infection; most cases are mild but some people develop severe illness.
suggested_tests: COVID-19 rapid antigen or RT-PCR test
self_care: Test if available and isolate while symptomatic
Rest, fluids and monitor symptoms
If you have a pulse oximeter, check oxygen saturation
see_doctor_if: Oxygen saturation below 94% or breathing difficulty
Persistent chest pain, confusion or bluish lips

conditions.name: Dengue fever
conditions.description: A mosquito-borne viral infection with high fever and severe aches; can become severe and needs monitoring.
suggested_tests: Complete blood count with platelet count
Dengue NS1 antigen / IgM antibody test
self_care: Rest and drink plenty of fluids (ORS, water, soups)
Avoid aspirin and ibuprofen-type pain killers unless a doctor advises otherwise - they can increase bleeding risk
Use mosquito protection to avoid spreading infection
see_doctor_if: Severe abdominal pain, persistent vomiting, bleeding gums/nose, blood in vomit or stool, restlessness - these are warning signs needing emergency care
Platelet count is falling

conditions.name: Malaria
conditions.description: A mosquito-borne parasitic infection causing fever with chills; needs a blood test and prompt treatment.
suggested_tests: Malaria rapid diagnostic test or blood smear
self_care: Get tested promptly - malaria can worsen within a day
Rest and stay hydrated
Use bed nets and repellents
see_doctor_if: Any fever with chills in an area where malaria occurs - get tested the same day
Confusion, drowsiness, breathing difficulty or dark urine

conditions.name: Typhoid (enteric) fever
conditions.description: A bacterial infection spread through contaminated food or water, causing prolonged fever and abdominal symptoms.
self_care: Drink safe, boiled or treated water
Eat freshly cooked food and wash hands
Do not self-medicate with leftover antibiotics
see_doctor_if: Fever lasting more than 3 days
Severe abdominal pain, blood in stool or confusion

conditions.name: Gastroenteritis (stomach infection)
conditions.description: Inflammation of the gut, usually from a virus or contaminated food, causing diarrhoea and/or vomiting.
suggested_tests: Usually none; stool test if prolonged or bloody
self_care: Sip oral rehydration solution (ORS) frequently
Eat light food as tolerated
Wash hands thoroughly to avoid spreading infection
see_doctor_if: Signs of dehydration: very little urine, dizziness on standing, dry mouth
Blood in stool, high fever, or symptoms beyond 3 days

conditions.name: Urinary tract infection (UTI)
conditions.description: A bacterial infection of the bladder or urinary tract, more common in women.
self_care: Drink plenty of water
Do not delay urination
see_doctor_if: Burning urination - a urine test can confirm infection and guide treatment
Fever, back/side pain or vomiting (possible kidney infection) - seek care promptly
You are pregnant

conditions.name: Type 2 diabetes / prediabetes
conditions.description: Raised blood sugar due to the body not using insulin effectively; often silent and detected on blood tests.
self_care: Choose whole grains, vegetables and pulses; limit sugary drinks and refined carbohydrates
Aim for at least 150 minutes of moderate activity per week
If overweight, even modest weight loss can improve blood sugar
see_doctor_if: Blood sugar results are above the normal range - a doctor should confirm with repeat testing
Very high thirst and urination with weight loss, vomiting or drowsiness - seek care promptly

conditions.name: High blood pressure (hypertension)
conditions.description: Persistently raised blood pressure that usually causes no symptoms but increases heart and stroke risk.
suggested_tests: Repeat blood pressure readings on different days (or home/ambulatory monitoring)
self_care: Reduce salt intake (WHO advises < 5 g per day)
Be physically active and keep a healthy weight
Limit alcohol and avoid tobacco
Measure blood pressure at home and keep a log
see_doctor_if: Readings are repeatedly 130/80 mmHg or above
Reading of 180/120 mmHg or higher, especially with chest pain, breathlessness, weakness or vision changes - emergency

conditions.name: Anaemia (possible iron deficiency)
conditions.description: Low haemoglobin reduces oxygen delivery; iron deficiency is the most common cause.
self_care: Include iron-rich foods (green leafy vegetables, legumes, jaggery, eggs, meat) with vitamin C sources
Avoid tea or coffee with meals as they reduce iron absorption
Take supplements only as advised by a doctor
see_doctor_if: Haemoglobin is below the normal range - the cause should be investigated
Breathlessness at rest, chest pain, fainting or any blood loss (e.g. black stools, heavy periods)

conditions.name: Underactive thyroid (hypothyroidism)
conditions.description: The thyroid gland makes too little hormone, slowing metabolism.
self_care: Keep a symptom diary to discuss with your doctor
Maintain a balanced diet and regular activity
see_doctor_if: TSH outside the reference range - a doctor should confirm and decide on treatment
You are pregnant or planning pregnancy

conditions.name: High cholesterol / blood lipids
conditions.description: Raised LDL cholesterol or triglycerides, a silent risk factor for heart disease and stroke.
self_care: Limit saturated and trans fats (fried foods, butter, ghee, processed meats)
Increase fibre: oats, pulses, vegetables, fruit
Exercise regularly and avoid tobacco
see_doctor_if: Lipids above target - your doctor can estimate overall heart risk and advise treatment

conditions.name: Asthma
conditions.description: A chronic airway condition causing episodes of wheeze, cough and breathlessness.
self_care: Avoid known triggers such as smoke, dust and cold air
If prescribed an inhaler, keep it with you and use as directed
Have a written asthma action plan
see_doctor_if: Recurrent wheeze or night-time cough
Severe breathlessness, difficulty speaking, or bluish lips - emergency

conditions.name: Pneumonia (lung infection)
conditions.description: An infection of the lungs causing cough, fever and breathing difficulty; needs medical assessment.
self_care: Rest and fluids while awaiting medical review
Do not take leftover antibiotics without prescription
see_doctor_if: Cough with fever and breathlessness - see a doctor promptly
Breathing difficulty, confusion, or oxygen saturation below 94% - emergency

conditions.name: Tuberculosis (TB) - needs testing
conditions.description: A bacterial infection usually of the lungs causing a prolonged cough; curable with a full course of treatment.
self_care: Cover your mouth when coughing and ventilate rooms
Get tested - TB is curable when treated fully
see_doctor_if: Cough lasting more than 2 weeks, especially with weight loss, night sweats or blood in sputum

conditions.name: Migraine / primary headache
conditions.description: Recurrent moderate-to-severe headaches, often one-sided, with nausea or light sensitivity.
suggested_tests: Usually clinical diagnosis; a headache diary helps
self_care: Rest in a dark, quiet room during attacks
Keep regular sleep and meals and stay hydrated
Track possible triggers in a headache diary
see_doctor_if: Headaches are frequent or changing in pattern
Sudden 'worst ever' headache, headache with fever and stiff neck, weakness, or confusion - emergency

conditions.name: Reduced kidney function
conditions.description: Kidneys filtering less effectively; often silent and found on blood tests.
self_care: Keep blood pressure and blood sugar well controlled
Avoid regular use of painkillers like NSAIDs without medical advice
Stay hydrated unless told to restrict fluids
see_doctor_if: Creatinine above the reference range
Very little urine, severe swelling or breathlessness - seek care urgently

conditions.name: Liver inflammation / dysfunction
conditions.description: Raised liver enzymes or bilirubin, which can come from fatty liver, alcohol, medicines or hepatitis.
self_care: Avoid alcohol
Do not take extra paracetamol or herbal supplements without advice
Maintain a healthy weight
see_doctor_if: Liver tests are abnormal or you notice yellow eyes or dark urine
Confusion, vomiting blood or severe abdominal pain - emergency

conditions.name: Vitamin D deficiency
conditions.description: Low vitamin D, common with limited sun exposure; can affect bones and muscles.
self_care: Safe daily sunlight exposure
Include vitamin D sources such as eggs, fish and fortified foods
Take supplements only at the dose your doctor advises
see_doctor_if: Vitamin D is below the reference range

conditions.name: Vitamin B12 deficiency
conditions.description: Low B12 can cause anaemia and nerve symptoms; more common in vegetarian diets.
self_care: Include B12 sources such as dairy, eggs, fish or fortified foods
see_doctor_if: B12 is low or you have persistent numbness or tingling

conditions.name: Low mood / possible depression - talk to a professional
conditions.description: Persistent low mood or loss of interest that affects daily life; effective help is available.
suggested_tests: Assessment by a doctor or mental health professional
Thyroid test to exclude physical causes
self_care: Talk to someone you trust about how you feel
Keep a regular routine with sleep, meals and some physical activity
Limit alcohol
see_doctor_if: Low mood lasting more than two weeks or affecting daily life
Any thoughts of self-harm - contact a crisis line or emergency services now
